The free speech and the layout. Reddit had a terrible layout and it looked like it was slapped together in 5 minutes. Voat is in alpha and still looks orders of magnitude better than Reddit. The community here is also much nicer and more discussion oriented.
The reason I see thus far... Aside from a few communities, the majority of people seem to be separated from an ideology and more into intelligent discussion.

It's been surprisingly easy to keep this environment with a small amount of people. I think the democratic format helps for that. Most people are willing to have a reasoned discussion. But when you put them in a populated space like reddit...suddenly they're surrounded by so many people who disagree with them, they can't help but get a little reactionary.

When you've got a group of individuals, they can communicate with words and generally be civil. When it's a group of communities who subscribe to individual ideologies, the communication is reduced to speaking out of bias, emotional reactions, using words that mean different things to different people, etc. Because every conversation they're having is an extension of an older conversation, usually one that already pissed them off. Makes for bitter, oversimplified comments.
